title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is an isolated, very sketchy fragment. The neighbouring pages are Bourbaki-style drafts on holomorphic functions and PDE, apparently filed with it by chance, so they give no context. The setting appears to be a Tannakian category C ('catégorie de Tannaka') together with an extra structure T, an object of some category I(C). Plausible readings of T are an invertible 'Tate' object, a fibre functor, or a rigidifying datum; the meaning of I(C) is not recoverable from this page. Underlined Eq(C) denotes the groupoid/2-group of autoequivalences of C, and Eq(C,T) those that respect T, with a forgetful functor Eq(C,T) -> Eq(C).

The argument runs as follows:
- Suppose one could attach T canonically to C, or rather to its equivalence class. Then one has lifted the canonical functor Eq(C,T) -> Eq(C) by a section c (the return arrow marked 'c').
- Consequently every C' equivalent to C receives a corresponding object T'_{C'} in I(C').
- Now take a triple (A', C', T') 'as above'. A' is presumably an extension of the coefficient ring, and (C,T)_{A'} the base-changed pair. The equivalences (C',T') ≃ (C,T)_{A'} form a category that is a torsor under Eq(C,T)_{A'} ≃ Eq(C',T').
- Passing to isomorphism classes gives a torsor under Bord(C',T'). 'Bord' seems to be the group of iso classes of autoequivalences, or a band/lien-type invariant.
- Dividing by the image of Bord(C) gives a torsor under Bord(C',T')/Im Bord(C). This torsor no longer depends on the choice of representative C in the equivalence class.
- It then remains to make explicit the canonical map Bord(C) -c-> Bord(C,T) -> Bord(C',T'), given by ρ ↦ (ρ, u_ρ) ↦ (ρ', u_ρ'). Here u_ρ lies in N_{0/A}(P_0), apparently built from a torsor P_0 attached to ρ by some norm-like or normaliser-like construction, and maps to N_{0/A'}(P'_0).

In modern terms this is a rigidification and descent problem. One wants to know whether a structured Tannakian category can be chosen canonically within its equivalence class, and the obstruction or indeterminacy is measured by a torsor under a quotient of automorphism groups. This is the kind of non-abelian-cohomology bookkeeping (gerbes, bands, 2-groups of autoequivalences) underlying the 1965 'Galois theory of motives' programme.
errors: No mathematical error can be identified; the page is a sketch with undefined notation (I(C), Bord, N_{0/A}, P_0). The torsor claims are standard-looking but are asserted without verification, and the canonical map Bord(C)->Bord(C',T') is left to be made explicit.

ideas.what: Groupoid (2-group) of autoequivalences of a Tannakian category, and of the category with extra structure T, with the forgetful functor between them
ideas.modern_name: Autoequivalence 2-group / automorphism gerbe of a Tannakian category
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra Rivano, 'Catégories tannakiennes' (LNM 265)

ideas.what: Equivalences between two structured categories form a torsor (category torsor, then set torsor on iso classes) under the automorphism 2-group; quotienting by the image of Bord(C) gives an invariant independent of the representative C
ideas.modern_name: Torsors/gerbes and bands in non-abelian cohomology; rigidification up to equivalence

ideas.what: Base change of a structured Tannakian category along a coefficient extension A -> A', i.e. (C,T)_{A'}
ideas.modern_name: Extension of scalars of Tannakian / linear categories

missed.claim: Grothendieck considers whether a structure T can be attached canonically to an equivalence class of Tannakian categories. He identifies the residual indeterminacy as a torsor under Bord(C',T')/Im Bord(C), then breaks off before computing the canonical map Bord(C)->Bord(C,T)->Bord(C',T').
missed.quote: Le torseur ne dépend plus du choix d'un C dans la classe de catégories envisagée.... Il faut donc expliciter l'application canonique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It shows early attention to canonicity and rigidification issues for motivic Tannakian categories over varying coefficient rings, later handled via gerbes and bands. The fragment is too sketchy to yield a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a fragmentary bookkeeping computation on autoequivalences and torsors for a structured Tannakian category. It is of historical interest as 1965 Tannakian-motivic work, but its content is standard non-abelian cohomology later systematised by Giraud and Saavedra. The notation is too undefined to extract a new statement.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'canoniquement' appears double-underlined, possibly an insertion rather than deleted; the reading is uncertain.
The superscript insertion above 'fonctions canoniques' is read as 'de Ext-cat' with a check mark; the reading is uncertain.
The arrow labelled 'c' is the return arrow Eq(C) -> Eq(C,T) (a section), drawn under the display.
'T'_{C'}' is written with the subscript resembling 'C'' (or 'ξ' superscript); 'I(C')' could also read 'V(C')' or 'J(C')'.
The last line shows 'N_{0/A}(P_0) ∋ u_ρ' and 'N_{0/A'}(P'_0) ∋ (u_ρ)''; the leftmost 'P_0' carries an '≃' mark above it.
Neighbouring pages (31, 29) belong to an unrelated Bourbaki analysis draft, apparently misfiled.
